tools.name: getBedrockRange
tools.description: Returns the Java version range Bedrock players can join, for fabric, neoforge and spigot (Paper and its forks); an empty string means unknown. Check it before enabling config.bedrockEnabled.

tools.name: listBills
tools.description: Lists past calendar months' bills, newest first, each with its cost per server. status pending means the month is closed but its bill is not final yet. Match each serverId to a name with listServers; a deleted server no longer appears there.

tools.name: getMonthSpending
tools.description: Breaks this calendar month's spend so far down by server: cost, compute cost and time awake. Match each serverId to a name with listServers and name servers by that name. For the total and the balance use getBalance.

tools.name: getLoaderVersions
tools.description: Lists the Minecraft versions each config.type can run, keyed by type. Use it before createServer or updateServer to choose config.version. VANILLA is omitted because it runs every version; a missing type means its list is unavailable.

tools.name: getPricingCatalog
tools.description: Returns estimated monthly prices in US cents, as the site shows them, for every available region and size under three play schedules (casual, regular, evenings), plus always-on host references when available. Name each size by its memoryGb, adding vcpu when two sizes share the same memory; the size

tools.name: listServers
tools.description: Lists the account's servers with id, name, join address, region, size, settings, state and recent disk, memory and lag figures. runtime.loadCause, when present, says why a server keeps lagging with players on: memory (garbage collection), cpu-starved (one core shared with background work; a second c

tools.name: createServer
tools.description: Creates a server, asleep and free until startServer or a joining player wakes it, and returns it with its id and join address. Region sets player latency and cannot change later: ask where players are if unknown; regions and size prices come from getPricingCatalog. Optional content from Modrinth, Cu

tools.name: deleteServer
tools.description: Permanently deletes the server with its world, settings, backups and exports, shutting it down if running. Call it only for a server the user named in this request, one server per call; for a request that names none or covers several, such as delete my servers, list them with listServers and ask whi

tools.name: updateServer
tools.description: Changes a server's name, size, settings, player lists, content, auto-start or custom domain. Omitted fields are kept, and a sent list replaces the stored one (uploaded files excepted). Not for the resource pack (setResourcePack) or a fresh world (resetServer). The returned server says when a restart

tools.name: startAssetUpload
tools.description: Only for an assistant that can send the user's file with HTTP PUT, such as a coding agent with a shell. Begins uploading one .jar or .zip mod, plugin, datapack or resource pack (up to 512 MiB, storage capped per server and account) and returns uploadId, key, fileName and parts: PUT each piece within

tools.name: abortAssetUploads
tools.description: Discards one or more (up to 50) unfinished or inspected uploads. Returns aborted and leftover. Installed files are removed with deleteAsset.

tools.name: completeAssetUploads
tools.description: Installs one or more (up to 50) files from startAssetUpload calls; resource packs go through setResourcePack. Files failing a check are returned in rejected with key and error; the rest apply at the next restart.

tools.name: inspectAssetUpload
tools.description: Completes a startAssetUpload and reports its kind, size and metadata without installing it. To install, pass it to completeAssetUploads, or setResourcePack with its key for a resource pack; abortAssetUploads discards it.

tools.name: deleteAsset
tools.description: Uninstalls a custom mod, plugin or datapack file that was uploaded to the server and deletes the file, taking effect at the next restart. The file can only be recovered from a backup.

tools.name: listBackups
tools.description: Lists backups newest first with backupId, startTime, sizeBytes, reason (daily, manual, upload, freeze, reset, config-change) and exportState (idle, exporting, ready). Pass backupId to restoreBackup, cancelBackupRestore, startBackupExport, getBackupDownloadUrl (exportState ready) or deleteBackup. Nam

tools.name: createBackup
tools.description: Takes a manual backup of the server's current world, which can later be restored or exported. Fails while the server is starting, stopping or restoring, before its first boot, or when the account balance is too low. Returns the backup as pending; listBackups shows it completed when done. Name a back

tools.name: deleteBackup
tools.description: Permanently deletes one backup; this cannot be undone. A backup that is queued for restore or being exported cannot be deleted. For the only remaining copy of a world the call is refused with requiresConfirmation; ask the user, then repeat with confirm true.

tools.name: getBackupDownloadUrl
tools.description: Returns a signed link, valid for 6 hours, to download a backup exported with startBackupExport. Fails if the export is not ready yet; requires a paid account. Returns url (a .tar.gz for the user) and expiresAt.

tools.name: deleteBackupExport
tools.description: Deletes the downloadable archive made by startBackupExport. The backup itself is kept and can be exported again.

tools.name: startBackupExport
tools.description: Packages a backup into a downloadable archive. Requires a paid account and balance; refused while another upload, export or restore is pending (at most 3 per account). Poll listBackups until exportState is ready, then call getBackupDownloadUrl; if it returns to idle instead, the export failed.

tools.name: cancelBackupRestore
tools.description: Cancels a restore from restoreBackup that an online server has not applied yet. Pass the queued backupId. Fails if nothing is queued for it or it is already being applied.

tools.name: restoreBackup
tools.description: Replaces the whole world with the chosen backup. No backup of the current world is taken, so everything since that backup is lost unless you run createBackup first. An asleep server restores at once; an online server applies it at the next restartServer or restartToApplySettings, and until then canc

tools.name: getConsoleLogs
tools.description: Returns up to 200 recent console lines, including startup, oldest first. Use it to see why a server failed to start or what happened in game; it cannot run commands. Returns events, nextCursor (newer) and prevCursor (older); platform notices are left out, so a page can hold fewer lines, or none, whi

tools.name: verifyCustomDomain
tools.description: Looks up the public DNS record of the custom domain set with updateServer customDomain and updates its status; use it after the user changes DNS. A record that points at the server verifies the domain and starts routing players to it. A failing record is reported with its reason and never takes a ve

tools.name: dismissJoinAttempt
tools.description: Clears the notice for a player the whitelist turned away; it does not whitelist, kick or ban. To let them in, add them to whitelist with updateServer. Returns the server.

tools.name: keepServerAwake
tools.description: Delays a running server's idle sleep by 5 minutes from now; it keeps being charged meanwhile. Use it while working on a server with no players online; to wake an asleep server use startServer. Fails with 409 if not running. Returns sleepAt.

tools.name: getServerMetrics
tools.description: Returns the server's load samples over the last minutes (default 30, up to 360), oldest first, one about every 30 seconds while it runs. Each point has its time, memory use, tick load in permille (divide by 20 for milliseconds per tick; 1000 means the server is lagging) and peak players. Gaps mean t

tools.name: deleteModpack
tools.description: Uninstalls the server's uploaded custom modpack and deletes the file, taking effect at the next restart. The world is kept, though the server may then suggest a world reset to clear content the pack left behind.

tools.name: startModpackUpload
tools.description: Only for an assistant that can send the user's file with HTTP PUT, such as a coding agent with a shell. Begins uploading a Modrinth .mrpack (up to 1 GiB). Returns uploadId, key, fileName and parts (url valid one hour): PUT each piece, keep each ETag, then completeModpackUpload. Refused when a modpac

tools.name: abortModpackUpload
tools.description: Cancels an unfinished, or checked but not yet installed, modpack upload and discards the file. An installed modpack is not affected; remove it with deleteModpack.

tools.name: completeModpackUpload
tools.description: Installs the .mrpack as the server's modpack, replacing loader, version and mods at the next restart; a backup is taken first. Pass uploadId, key and each ETag. Returns the server.

tools.name: inspectModpackUpload
tools.description: Completes a startModpackUpload and returns its version, loader and contents without installing. To install, call completeModpackUpload with the same arguments; abortModpackUpload discards it.

tools.name: resetServer
tools.description: Replaces the world with a fresh one, keeping settings, content and address; for an earlier world use restoreBackup instead. A running server disconnects its players and comes back online on the new world. A reset backup of the current world is taken first and earlier backups are kept, but the archiv

tools.name: setResourcePack
tools.description: Sets the resource pack players are offered on join, from Modrinth, an uploaded .zip or a link; from: none removes it. It applies at the next restart (restartToApplySettings). Make it mandatory with resourcePackRequired in updateServer. Returns the server.

tools.name: restartServer
tools.description: Reboots a running server's machine; players are disconnected for a minute or two while it boots and fetches its content from Modrinth, CurseForge or their download links. Use it for a pending size change or a stuck server; for changed game settings use restartToApplySettings. A restore queued with r

tools.name: restartToApplySettings
tools.description: Restarts only the Minecraft program on an online server so changed settings apply; players drop for a few seconds while it reloads content from Modrinth, CurseForge or their download links. Use it when the server reports a restart is required; for a size change use restartServer. If a pending change

tools.name: startServer
tools.description: Wakes an asleep server so players can join it from the internet at its address; not for an online server (use restartServer). While booting it fetches its mods, plugins and modpack from Modrinth, CurseForge or their download links, and a backup queued with restoreBackup replaces the current world. S

tools.name: stopServer
tools.description: Shuts a running server down so it sleeps, disconnecting players and ending running charges; world and settings are kept. For a reboot use restartServer. While autoStartEnabled is on, a joining player wakes it (turn off with updateServer). Returns the server.

tools.name: startWorldUpload
tools.description: Only for an assistant that can send the user's file with HTTP PUT, such as a coding agent with a shell. Begins uploading a world archive (.zip, .tar.gz, .tgz; up to 4 GiB). Returns jobId, uploadId, key and parts (partNumber, url valid one hour): PUT each piece to its url, keep each ETag, then call c

tools.name: abortWorldUpload
tools.description: Cancels an unfinished world upload and discards the parts uploaded so far. The server's current world is not affected. Only before completeWorldUpload.

tools.name: completeWorldUpload
tools.description: Call after every piece is uploaded, with jobId, uploadId, key and each ETag. The current world is not changed: the archive is imported in the background (minutes) into a new backup with reason upload in listBackups. To play it, run restoreBackup with that backupId. Fails over 4 GiB or on low balance

tools.name: refreshWorldUploadParts
tools.description: Returns new one-hour links for pieces of a startWorldUpload whose links expired. Pass jobId, uploadId, key and the pieces still to upload.

tools.name: getServerUsage
tools.description: Returns the time the server spent with at least one player online in its latest unbroken run on its current size (its last 7 days with players, or more days back until they hold 8 hours), histograms of CPU, tick load, GC pause share, memory peak, the JVM's live set and memory outside its heap over t

tools.name: getBalance
tools.description: Shows the signed-in user's balance, this month's spend so far and projected total, and what awake servers cost per hour. Call it when the user asks about their balance or spending. It cannot add funds. When the user asks to add funds: show the balance and addFunds with a link to dashboardUrl, and no

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "getPricingCatalog" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
